keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The page describes the fortress and the suburbs of Upe (Tranqueira), Hilir and Sabba, and 'does not describe a wider Portuguese territory' (it names no hinterland, Muar or Naning); the infobox gives no area. Cliopatria draws the same three cells (about 759 km2, 102.2-102.36E, 2.2-2.36N) inside its Portuguese Empire row in 1512-1571 and Portuguese Colonies 1564-1581 and 1640-1647, but its Portuguese Colonies shape of 1600-1635 has no Malacca cells and the Portuguese Empire row has no shape in 1600 (found by cell test).

ledger.note: 24 August 1511: Albuquerque takes Malacca. 'Malacca fell to the Portuguese on 24 August with Sultan Mahmud Shah fleeing the city'; Albuquerque sailed from Goa in April 1511 with about 1,200 men and 17 or 18 ships and stayed until November to prepare the defences. The infobox gives 15 August 1511 instead (a discrepancy on the page).

wars.outcome: The city fell on 24 August 1511 and Mahmud Shah fled; the Portuguese built a fortress and held the city for 130 years.
wars.note: The page's infobox says 15 August; the text 24 August.

wars.name: Javanese and Johor attacks on Malacca
wars.outcome: Failed: Sultan Mahmud with Demak naval support (1511), a second Demak campaign (1521), and in 1550 Johor's request to Java brought Ratu Kalinyamat's '4,000 soldiers aboard 40 ships'. The city did not change hands; in 1526 the Portuguese razed Bintan.

wars.name: Aceh attacks on Malacca
wars.outcome: Failed: 1568 (Aceh), 1573-1575 (Aceh and Jepara together, 'largely from poor coordination') and 1629 (Iskandar Muda with several hundred ships; Portuguese sources say about 19,000 men were lost).

wars.name: Dutch sieges and capture of Malacca

zones.text: Malacca town: the fortress (Fortaleza) and the suburbs of Upe (Tranqueira), Hilir and Sabba, the only land the page describes

wars.outcome: The Dutch siege of 1606 ended in a rout at the Battle of Cape Rachado and 'rallied the forces of the Sultanate of Johor into an alliance with the Dutch'; the Dutch attacked again in 1616 and, with Johor and Aceh, captured the city in January 1641.
wars.note: The Dutch-Portuguese War page adds 'In 1615, a battle off the coast of Malacca destroyed Portuguese naval power in Southeast Asia'.

certainty.note: The page describes a fortress city and its suburbs and no boundary; the three-cell outline is a city, not a frontier.

notes: Written 2026-10-24 by the se-03-x additions batch. A city colony Cliopatria lacks as a state (its cells sit inside the Portuguese Empire and Portuguese Colonies rows). One page cited for events (Portuguese Malacca); the Dutch-Portuguese War page is listed because a war note quotes it. Unsettled: (1) conquest date 15 August (infobox) or 24 August 1511 (text); month 8 either way. (2) The page gives no wider territory: the outline is the town only (no Muar, Naning, Bukit China hinterland; the page calls Bukit China only a suburb). (3) No rulers strip: the page's captains table runs 1512-1641 with gaps and two entries (56, 57) out of date order. (4) The sultan's fall belongs to sultanate-of-malacca (it records the loss to portuguese-empire); the counterpart string here is that dossier's slug. (5) The Portuguese Colonies review (sa-06) should note that Cliopatria's 1582-1639 shape lacks Malacca while the Portuguese held it. (6) The Bintan raid of 1526 and Johor's rise are for sultanate-of-johor and kingdom-of-bintan.
